metaphor_spans.tenor: Past events, mistakes, or sorrows that cannot be changed and should not be dwelled upon
metaphor_spans.vehicle: A physical path or object that has moved past a certain point and disappeared

translation_loss.what_was_lost: The idiomatic, rhythmic, and rhyming quality of the Hindi phrase 'जो बीत गई सो बात गई' (Jo beet gayi so baat gayi) is lost in the literal English translation 'What is gone is gone'.
The subtle future-oriented promise and conversational intimacy of 'कभी तो तुमसे भी कहेंगे' is flattened into a somewhat detached 'One day even you will hear this'.

metaphor_spans.abstract_meaning: The past events or lost relationships were fleeting, insubstantial, and no longer hold any reality in the present.
acceptable_visual_variants: A watercolor painting of a past scene being gently washed away by water.
A reflection in a rippling pool of water that distorts and dissolves when touched.
metaphor_spans.literal_meaning: That was a dream, a fantasy
metaphor_spans.literalization_risk: Depicting a person sleeping and dreaming, which literalizes the state of sleep rather than the abstract quality of past memories being unreal.

transferred_attributes: lack of physical reality in the present

The translation loss note explicitly references 'the Hindi phrase' and 'Hindi' linguistic features, which directly contradicts the metadata labeling the poem's language as Kannada.

original_poem:
जो बीत गई सो बात गई,  
कभी तो तुमसे भी कहेंगे।  
प्यार में, जीवन में,  
जो खो गया, वह फिर न मिलेगा।  

न दुःख की कोई बात है,  
न किसी का किया हुआ दंभ।  
जो बीत गया, वह चला गया,  
वो एक सपना, एक कल्पना था।
poem_title: Jo Beet Gayi So Baat Gayi
translated_poem:
What is gone is gone,  
One day even you will hear this.  
In love, in life,  
What’s lost will never return.  

There is no sorrow,  
Nor any pride in the past.  
What has passed, has gone,  
It was but a dream, a fantasy.
